title: Auction Module
summary: Auction listings, per-bidder bids, highest-bid tracking, time-driven expiration, and sale/win/loss notifications.
requirements: Create listings and accept bids on valid, unfinished listings.
Keep only each bidder's latest accepted bid; a bidder's replacement bid updates only when higher.
On expiration, determine sale/no-sale and notify seller, winner, and other bidders.
Use simulated time from rama-helpers for expiration checks.
nonfunctional: Listings and bids are visible within 5 milliseconds of their API calls.
Expiration is driven automatically by time in production.
constraints: process-expirations! is testing-only: it triggers handling of currently expired listings and waits; it does not replace automatic expiration.
invariants: A finished listing does not accept further bids.
At most one current bid per bidder per listing.
acceptance: get-listings returns creation-ordered listing maps with listing ID, item, and expiration time.
get-bids returns one latest amount per bidder; get-highest-bid returns {:user-id, :amount} or nil.
Expired auctions produce the documented seller :sale or :no-sale result and bidder :won or :lost results.
environment: Rama module with stream and microbatch topologies.
rama-helpers simulated time and TopologyScheduler expiration support.
interfaces: auction-module.protocol/AuctionModule: list-item!, bid!, get-listings, get-bids, get-highest-bid, get-notifications, process-expirations!
create-module returns :module and :wrap-client; client also implements harness/Synchronizable.
decisions: Reference depots: *listing-depot (hash by :user-id), *bid-depot (hash by nested-listing-user-id), and tick depot *expire-tick (30,000 ms unless shared/REPLACE-TICK-DEPOTS).
Reference stream topology auction maintains $$user-listings, $$listing-bidders, $$listing-top-bid, and $$user-bids; expirations microbatch maintains $$finished-listings and $$notifications.
Reference uses a TopologyScheduler to schedule listing expiration and handle due listings when ticks arrive.
tradeoffs: Reference stores listing/bidder views for direct reads and tracks top bid separately for a direct highest-bid lookup.
The documented production timer behavior is distinct from the testing-only explicit expiration trigger.
seam: No external module dependency is declared in the reference module.
etls: auction (stream): consumes listing and bid events; expirations (microbatch): schedules listings and handles expiration ticks.
queries: No named query topology is declared; client reads use foreign PState selections.

write: list-item! appends *listing-depot; auction stores seller listing; expirations schedules its listing ID and expiration.
bid! appends *bid-depot; auction checks $$finished-listings, updates bidder/latest and top-bid state, and records bidder history.
Expiration tick invokes scheduler handling; marks listing finished and appends seller and bidder results to $$notifications.
read: Client directly selects listings, bidder rows, top bid, and notifications from PStates; notifications are converted to protocol maps.
flow.partition: Listings are depot-partitioned by seller user-id; bids by the user-id embedded in listing-id. Reference selects listing-scoped bid state with the listing owner as PState partition key.

caveat: The protocol specifies behavior and simulated time. Component names and the 30-second tick are reference choices.

title: Bank Transfer Module
summary: Tracks account balances and incoming/outgoing transfer history, applying successful transfers across user partitions.
requirements: Support deposits and transfers; report balances and per-user transfer history.
A transfer succeeds only when the source has sufficient balance; successful transfers debit source and credit destination.
nonfunctional: Processing must be fault-tolerant: successful appends must neither be lost nor double-processed.
constraints: The same transfer ID is guaranteed never to be appended twice.
invariants: Failed transfers do not change balances.
Incoming and outgoing history records expose transfer ID, amount, counterparty, and success flag.
acceptance: get-balance returns current balance or zero for a user with no deposits.
Outgoing entries have {:to-user-id, :amt, :success?}; incoming entries have {:from-user-id, :amt, :success?}.
Transfer processing is retry/failure safe under the stated uniqueness assumption.
environment: Rama module using a microbatch topology; client synchronization waits for processed batches.
interfaces: create-module returns :module and :wrap-client; client implements harness/Synchronizable.
decisions: Reference depots: *deposit-depot partitioned by :user-id; *transfer-depot partitioned by :from-user-id.
Reference microbatch topology banking maintains $$funds, $$outgoing-transfers, and $$incoming-transfers.
Reference checks source balance, writes outgoing history, routes to destination partition, and credits destination only on success.
tradeoffs: Reference processes source debit and destination credit in one microbatch flow while explicitly repartitioning to the recipient.
The no-duplicate-ID assumption supplies transfer identity uniqueness; it does not remove the stated fault-tolerance requirement.
seam: No external module dependency is declared in the reference module.
etls: banking (microbatch): consumes deposits and transfers, updates balances and both transfer histories.
queries: No named query topology; client reads use foreign PState selections.

write: deposit! appends *deposit-depot; banking adds the amount to $$funds.
transfer! appends *transfer-depot; banking tests available funds and writes outgoing status, conditionally debits, routes to recipient, conditionally credits, and writes incoming status.
read: Client selects balance with zero default or selects all incoming/outgoing history for the user.
flow.partition: Reference deposit events hash by user-id and transfer events by source user-id; successful transfer processing hashes by destination user-id before recipient-side state access.

caveat: The contract does not mandate microbatching, depot/PState names, or ordering of returned history vectors.

title: Chat App
summary: Chat with rooms, membership, threaded messages, presence, unread counts, mentions and recent-thread feeds.
requirements: Support globally unique user handles and room names; profiles and membership; room messages and threaded replies.
Derive unread counts, mention inbox, recent-thread feeds, and presence.
Reject user-initiated writes other than register! for unregistered users; reject nonmember messages/replies without effects.
Parse mentions as @ tokens ending at whitespace, period, or end; resolve only registered handles.
nonfunctional: Registration, profile, room create, and accepted room messages meet 5 ms visibility bounds specified by the protocol.
Room-member pages, room/thread pages, recent threads, unread counts, and mention pages target approximately 50 ms; specified history reads have fixed-work bounds.
Heartbeats arrive around 100,000/s; reads dominate at thousands/s; total stated workload also includes 2,000 messages/replies/s and 100/s registrations and room membership changes.
constraints: User and room IDs are Long; handles, names, titles, room names, and content are strings.
A user belongs to at most 1,000 rooms; rooms may contain 50,000 members; message content has at most 10 mentions; thread at most 1,000 distinct participants.
Presence is online for heartbeat within 120 seconds and may be imperfectly reliable.
Leaving discards read position; later rejoin treats current messages as unread; authored messages remain.
invariants: Concurrent claims for a handle or room name yield exactly one successful ID and no partial effects for losers.
Joining/leaving is idempotent; unknown room join has no effect.
Thread replies do not appear in room pages; reply makes replier a participant and starter is a participant from start.
Unread counts count room messages only, after last read marker; thread replies excluded.
acceptance: Unique registration/room creation, registration gates, message membership gates, pagination/order/shapes, and protocol-defined visibility behavior are honored.
Room and thread pages return at most 20 newest-before-cursor entries; recent threads return at most 20, with only 200 most recently active threads visible.
Unread counts cover current memberships and are O(1) per room; mentions and room/thread/recent-thread history reads are bounded as specified.
environment: Rama module with stream topology core, microbatch topology derived, query topologies, and task-global presence object.
interfaces: chat-app.protocol/ChatApp: register!, set-profile!, heartbeat!, create-room!, join-room!, leave-room!, post-message!, reply-in-thread!, mark-room-read!, registered?, lookup-handle, lookup-room, get-profile, get-presence, get-room-members, get-online-members, get-room-page, get-thread-page, get-recent-threads, get-unread-counts, get-mentions-page
create-module returns :module and :wrap-client; client implements harness/Synchronizable.
decisions: *register-depot routes by handle; *user-actions-depot by user-id. core handles durable low-latency writes; derived builds asynchronous views.

core owns $$handles, $$users, $$room-names, $$rooms, $$profiles, $$room-messages and $$thread-replies. derived owns $$room-members, $$user-rooms, $$room-seq, $$read-cursors, $$room-reply-counts, $$thread-meta, $$thread-participants, $$mentions, $$rt-by-act and $$rt-idx.
Task-global *presence holds presence timestamps. Query topologies: heartbeat, presence, room-page, thread-page, recent-threads, unread-counts, mentions-page and online-filter.
tradeoffs: Per-room sequence numbers and per-user read cursors give O(1)-per-room unread counts.
Durable messages are separate from derived views, which the protocol allows to update asynchronously.
get-online-members scans membership in chunks of 256 through online-filter; collecting 20 online members may take several chunks.
seam: No external module dependency is declared in the reference module.
etls: core (stream): claims registrations and room names, stores profiles/messages/replies, routes user actions.
derived (microbatch): materializes membership, unread, thread, mention, and recent-thread views.

write: Registration claims handle and then records user; other actions route through user-action depot and registration checks.
Accepted messages are stored in room or thread PState; derived processing resolves mentions and updates unread/thread views.
Heartbeat mutates task-global presence through heartbeat query.
read: Lookup/profile/member/page/unread/mentions/recent-thread client methods select local state or invoke corresponding query topology; presence invokes presence query.
flow.partition: Reference partitions registration by handle and actions by acting user; room messages/membership by room; user views by user; thread replies and metadata by root UUID. Cross-key paths explicitly hash to the relevant key.

caveat: Presence expires after 30 seconds in the reference versus 120 seconds in the protocol. Component names, core/derived split, schemas and chunk sizes are reference choices; workload and method semantics are contractual.

title: Fanout
summary: Profiles, posts and bounded per-user timelines, using a separately deployed social graph.
requirements: Publish posts to poster's own timeline and each follower's timeline; provide complete chronological own-post history.
Deliver fanout in balanced, fair chunks; every post's fanout eventually completes.
Do not write durable PState/depot records per follower; per-follower delivery writes may be in-memory only.
Recover in-memory timeline state after worker restart through another mechanism.
nonfunctional: Profile visible within 5 ms; own post appears in poster's user-timeline within 5 ms.
Follower/self timeline fanout may be asynchronous, up to one second for users without huge follower counts.
Normal timeline page work is fixed and about 50 ms; only latest 800 entries visible.
constraints: Assume heavily unbalanced graph: most users fewer than 100 followers, some millions.
Assume a user posts no more than once every 5 seconds.
Must run alongside provided fanout.social-graph/SocialGraphModule, which is not included in this module's create-module result.
invariants: Timeline page is at most 20 entries, newest first, strictly before UUID7 cursor; names are poster's current profile name.
Recovered timeline may include posts from before follow and may omit already-delivered entries from subsequently unfollowed accounts.
acceptance: Protocol behavior for profiles, posts, own timeline and paged timeline is satisfied.
Fanout is balanced/fair/eventually complete and avoids durable per-follower writes; normal timeline read is fixed-work.
environment: Rama module composed with fanout.social-graph/SocialGraphModule via PState mirrors; stream writes, microbatch fanout, query topologies, task-global cache.
interfaces: fanout.protocol/Fanout: set-profile!, get-profile, post!, get-user-timeline, get-timeline-page
create-module returns this module only and :wrap-client; client implements harness/Synchronizable.
decisions: *profile-depot and *post-depot accept writes; $$mirror-control, $$mirror-followers and $$mirror-followees mirror the social graph.
writes stores $$profiles and $$user-posts; fanout uses $$pending-fanouts and task-global *cache.
Queries: get-user-timeline, compute-timeline-init, reconstruct-timeline and get-timeline. Fanout processes current and pending follower chunks separately.
tradeoffs: Durable posts and pending cursors avoid per-recipient durable writes. Timelines are reconstructed in memory from post and social-graph state.
The cache holds 800 entries; MAX-FOLLOWERS-PER-TASK-PER-MB=1000 bounds each chunk.
seam: Consumes fanout.social-graph/SocialGraphModule; reference mirrors its $$partitioned-followers-control, $$partitioned-followers, and $$user-followees.
etls: fanout (microbatch): processes posts and pending follower chunks; delivers grouped entries to in-memory cache.

write: post! appends *post-depot; writes stores post; fanout obtains followers from mirrored social-graph state and advances chunk cursors in $$pending-fanouts; grouped deliveries reach initialized in-memory timelines.
read: Own-post query selects $$user-posts. Timeline query initializes missing cache from followees and recent posts, reads recent cache entries, and resolves current profile/content.
flow.partition: Reference hashes poster ID to $$mirror-control, directly routes to each social-graph follower task, and hashes poster/user IDs for local state access. Exact source PState partition contract is not specified in challenge text.

caveat: The challenge names the SocialGraph module and mirror PStates. Cache layout, chunk size, topology names and recovery strategy are reference choices.

title: Social Graph and Fanout
summary: Combines social graph materialization with scalable post delivery and paginated per-user timelines.
requirements: Materialize follow/followee relations and profiles; process posts into timelines.
Balance CPU across tasks and keep aggregate disk work within a small constant factor of minimum for any follower distribution.
Fanout cannot write to durable PState/depot per follower; per-follower delivery is in-memory only.
Fanout must be fair, eventually complete, and fault-tolerant despite in-memory state loss on restart.
nonfunctional: Profiles visible within 5 ms; poster's own timeline visible within 5 ms; follower fanout may be asynchronous up to one second for non-huge follower sets.
Timeline read fixed-work, roughly 50 ms normally, independent of follows/posts; recovery may be slower.
Workload: ~7,000 posts/s, ~100 follows/unfollows/s; account follows no more than 5,000 others.
constraints: IDs are Long; name, location, content are strings.
Follow/unfollow idempotent; graph views consistent within processing barrier.
Only latest 800 timeline entries visible; recovered timeline may include pre-follow posts or omit entries after unfollow.
invariants: Each post creates one timeline entry per follower and one for author.
Timeline pages contain up to 20 most recent entries before UUID7 cursor; poster name is current profile name.
Follower/followee queries return current sets, empty when absent.
acceptance: Protocol behavior for idempotent graph updates, profiles, posts, own history and paged timeline is met.
Fanout balancing, fairness, eventual completion, no durable per-follower delivery, and stated normal read cost are satisfied for arbitrary distributions.
environment: Single Rama module with stream topologies social-graph and writes, microbatch topology fanout, queries, and task-global timeline cache.
interfaces: social-graph-and-fanout.protocol/SocialApp: follow!, unfollow!, set-profile!, post!, get-followers, get-followees, get-profile, get-user-timeline, get-timeline-page
create-module returns :module and :wrap-client; client implements harness/Synchronizable.
decisions: Reference depots: *follow-depot, *profile-depot, *post-depot, *process-tick.

Reference graph PStates: $$partitioned-followers-control, $$partitioned-follower-tasks, $$partitioned-followers, $$user-followees; writes PStates $$profiles and $$user-posts; fanout PState $$pending-fanouts; task-global *cache.
Reference query topologies: get-followers, get-user-timeline, compute-timeline-init, reconstruct-timeline, get-timeline.
Reference assigns follower partitions in increments of NEW-TASK-CUTOFF=1000 and processes up to MAX-FOLLOWERS-PER-TASK-PER-MB=1000 per task per batch.
tradeoffs: Reference distributes a high-follower target's follower set across tasks, while control and follower-to-task mappings support discovery and unfollow.
Durable post/graph state enables timeline reconstruction; in-memory ring buffers avoid per-follower durable writes.
Reference reconstructs from a limited set of followees and recent posts; protocol explicitly relaxes timeline exactness during recovery.
seam: No external module dependency; social graph PStates and fanout are within this module.
etls: social-graph (stream): materializes partitioned followers and inverse followees.
writes (stream): stores profiles and user posts.
fanout (microbatch): processes post follower chunks and updates in-memory timeline cache.

write: follow!/unfollow! appends *follow-depot; social-graph updates inverse followees and distributed follower sets.
post! appends *post-depot; writes persists author post; fanout chunks follower partitions, tracks continuation, and delivers in-memory grouped entries.
read: Graph getters read follower query or followee PState; own timeline reads stored posts; timeline page reconstructs missing cache then resolves post content and current profile.
flow.partition: Reference hashes target to follower control and uses direct task routing for partitioned follower state; user-followees keyed by follower account. Post fanout routes to graph task IDs recorded in control.

caveat: Random task allocation, cutoffs, cache and query/topology names are reference choices. Performance and fault-tolerance requirements apply across arbitrary follower distributions.

title: Time Series Module Hard
summary: Aggregates render-latency measurements into multi-granularity windows to answer minute-range statistics efficiently.
requirements: Record URL render latency with timestamp.
Return cardinality, total, minimum, and maximum over half-open minute-bucket range [start,end).
Efficiently handle both small and multi-year ranges with no unnecessary disk reads.
nonfunctional: get-stats-for-range must be efficient for every range size.
constraints: Range uses minute buckets and is half-open.
Challenge leaves depot, PState, and topology names to implementation.
invariants: Aggregates combine cardinality and total by addition and min/max across nonempty measurements.
Empty results have cardinality and total zero and nil min/max in reference representation.
acceptance: For any URL and half-open minute range, return correct {:cardinality, :total, :min-latency-millis, :max-latency-millis} aggregate.
Large ranges must use efficient aggregated retrieval rather than scanning all minute buckets.
environment: Rama module with microbatch ETL and query topology; client synchronization waits on timeseries microbatch.
interfaces: create-module returns :module and :wrap-client; client implements harness/Synchronizable.
decisions: Reference depot *render-latency-depot hashes by :url; microbatch topology timeseries updates $$window-stats.
Reference stores WindowStats at minute (:m), hour (:h), day (:d), and 30-day (:td) granularities; query topology get-stats-for-range decomposes request into aligned ranges across levels.
tradeoffs: Reference writes each sample into four granularities to reduce reads for large ranges; queries combine selected coarse buckets with finer boundary ranges.
The hierarchy's 60-minute, 24-hour, and 30-day conversion and names are reference design choices, not specified contract details.
seam: No external module dependency is declared in the reference module.
etls: timeseries (microbatch): consumes latency events and aggregates them into each time granularity.

write: record-latency! appends *render-latency-depot; timeseries computes bucket IDs and combines a single-measurement stat at each granularity.
read: get-stats-for-range partitions by URL, decomposes minute range into coarse aligned and fine boundary ranges, selects bucket values, and combines them.
flow.partition: Reference depot and PState are keyed by URL; query hashes URL before local range selections.

caveat: The contract requires correct, efficient half-open range queries. Granularity levels and schema names are reference choices.

title: Unbalanced Social Graph
summary: Materializes follower and followee relationships in a distribution-independent layout suitable for balanced downstream fanout.
requirements: Maintain idempotent follow/unfollow relationships and expose followers and followees.
Keep task CPU balanced and disk work near-optimal within a small constant factor across arbitrary follower distributions.
Design depots/PStates for direct consumption by a separate fanout module, which does not call this protocol.
nonfunctional: Target workload: ~7,000 posts/s, ~100 follows/unfollows/s; no account follows more than 5,000 others.
Near-optimality must hold for heavy-tailed, mid-heavy, flat, and other distributions.
constraints: Account and target IDs are Long.
Follower counts may range from small numbers to millions; distribution is not fixed.
Client writes are consistent by wait-for-processing barrier.
invariants: get-followers and get-followees return current sets, empty when no relations exist.
acceptance: Protocol graph operations return correct current sets after processing.
Layout supports balanced/resource-efficient downstream fanout for any distribution, not a single tuned distribution.
environment: Rama module with social-graph stream topology and get-followers query topology.
interfaces: create-module returns :module and :wrap-client; client implements harness/Synchronizable.
decisions: Reference depot *follow-depot hashes by :account-id.
Reference PStates: $$partitioned-followers-control, $$partitioned-follower-tasks, $$partitioned-followers, $$user-followees.
Reference social-graph stream updates inverse followees, allocates each follower to a task, and routes directly; get-followers gathers follower partitions.
tradeoffs: Reference distributes large follower sets among tasks, with a control list and follower-to-task lookup to enable reads and removals.
Reference NEW-TASK-CUTOFF is 1000 and task allocation method is a reference implementation choice, not a protocol requirement.
seam: Fanout module reads depots/PStates directly; it does not use the SocialGraph protocol. Exact compatible source identifiers are therefore relevant to composition.
etls: social-graph (stream): consumes follow events and updates partitioned follower and inverse followee views.

write: follow! / unfollow! append follow events; social-graph updates inverse followee set and routes follower add/remove to assigned task.
read: get-followers invokes query that reads control task list, gathers follower sets from listed tasks, and aggregates a set; get-followees selects inverse view.
flow.partition: Reference hashes target ID to control/lookup state, directs to assigned follower task, and hashes account ID for inverse followees. The exact strategy is reference-specific; contract requires balanced access for downstream fanout.

caveat: The README requires direct depot/PState interoperability with fanout. Component names come from the reference; the protocol does not prescribe them.
